title: Following Jesus: What Do the Sources Ask?
subtitle: Jesus's worship and moral practice compared with Islamic and Christian life
summary: Christians and Muslims both claim to honor Jesus. The most useful comparison is not a contest over labels but an examination of his worship: he prayed to God, submitted his will, fasted, gave charity, lived modestly, and affirmed the one Lord. Islam presents these practices as the continuing way of all prophets and directs worship to the God Jesus worshiped.

seo.metaTitle: Following Jesus: What Do the Sources Ask?
seo.metaDescription: Belief, worship, and practice in following Jesus, and why Islam connects love for the Messiah with devotion to his God.

sections.title: Follow His Worship, Not Just His Appearance
sections.body:
Islam offers a substantive claim to continuity with Jesus: direct worship of God, obedience, repentance, prayer, and care for others. It does not prove that claim by counting similarities in clothing or diet.

The harder question is whether Jesus authorized the Christian understanding of his identity or whether the Quran reliably restores his prophetic mission. Love of Jesus makes that investigation more important, not less.

sections.title: A Question of Loyalty, Not a Contest Between Neighbors
sections.body:
A generous Christian may imitate Jesus's character better than a selfish Muslim. That observation neither proves nor disproves either religion. The question concerns the teaching we should follow, not which community can claim every good person.

Jesus's prayer and obedience provide a positive starting point for Islam. To investigate the Christian explanation of that same evidence, read [Did Jesus Worship God?](/articles/did-jesus-worship-god).

sections.title: Whom Did Jesus Worship?
sections.body: Jesus taught the greatest commandment as, 'The Lord our God, the Lord is one' (Mark 12:29). He prayed, fasted, submitted his will, and called people to obey God. Christianity explains this as the human life of God the Son. Islam sees the straightforward pattern of a human messenger worshiping the Creator who sent him.

sections.title: Jesus in a Prophetic Tradition
sections.body: Jesus lived within the monotheistic tradition of Abraham and Moses. His worship was not detached spirituality: it included prayer, scripture, fasting, charity, moral discipline, and obedience. The Quran places Muhammad in the same prophetic line and describes the true disciples of Jesus as people who submitted themselves to God.

sections.title: The Quranic Jesus: Messiah and Servant
sections.body: The Quran records the disciples saying, 'We have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims [those who submit]' (Quran 3:52). It also presents Jesus saying that God commanded him to pray and give charity throughout his life (19:31). Islam does not reduce Jesus by calling him a servant of God. Service to the Creator is the highest human honor, and Jesus models it perfectly.

sections.title: Jesus's Worship in the Gospels
sections.body: The Gospels portray Jesus praying through the night (Luke 6:12), falling on his face and submitting his will to God (Matthew 26:39), fasting (Matthew 4:2), and affirming the one Lord (Mark 12:29). He says, 'My Father is greater than I' (John 14:28) and calls the Father 'the only true God' while describing himself as the one sent (John 17:3). Christians interpret these through incarnation; Muslims read them as direct evidence of prophethood.

sections.title: What the Resemblances Actually Show
sections.body:
Prayer, fasting, charity, and submission to God make Islamic worship recognizable within the prophetic pattern. They show that Muslim devotion is not alien to the way the Gospels portray Jesus.

They cannot by themselves establish Muhammad's prophethood or the Quran's authority. Muslims also follow the guidance given through Muhammad rather than trying to reconstruct every first-century custom. The Islamic claim is continuity in worship of the same Creator under His guidance, not identical ritual details in every age.

sections.title: The Strong Christian Reply: The New Covenant
sections.body:
Christians do not normally think that changes in diet or ritual abandon Jesus. They believe his mission, death, and resurrection establish a new covenant and that the apostles faithfully explain its implications. On that view, following Jesus includes trusting who he is, not merely copying his earthly habits.

Islam disputes that theological account and gives priority to Jesus's submission to the God who sent him, confirmed by the Quran. That disagreement must be argued through revelation and identity. A beard, a head covering, or abstention from pork cannot settle it.

sections.title: A Positive Way to Remain Loyal to Jesus
sections.body:
Islam invites you to keep love for the Messiah while directing worship as he did: to God. It places prayer, charity, moral discipline, and repentance in ordinary daily life, so honoring a prophet becomes lived obedience rather than praise alone.

That invitation also judges Muslims. Claiming to follow the prophets while mistreating family, neglecting the poor, or lying about another faith contradicts the character the claim requires.

sections.title: Move From Resemblance to Reasons
sections.body:
Read a prayer of Jesus and ask whether your own devotion has the same direction. Then examine the harder question: what grounds could establish that Muhammad continues God's guidance?

[Who Is Prophet Muhammad?](/articles/who-is-prophet-muhammad) is the next step. It addresses the authority a case from shared practices alone cannot supply.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Does comparing religious practice imply that Christians do not follow Jesus?
A: No. Many Christians sincerely imitate Jesus. The comparison asks which theology and worship pattern most directly continue his submission to the one God.

Q: If Muslims do not worship Jesus, why do they pray the way he prayed?
A: Islam shares Jesus's direction of worship and includes prostration, fasting, and charity. That does not establish identical rituals in every detail. Muslims follow Muhammad's guidance while understanding the core worship as continuous with earlier prophets.

Q: Did Jesus eat pork?
A: The Gospels do not record him eating pork, and his Jewish setting gives reason to expect abstention. Christians interpret later New Testament teaching as authorizing changed food rules. Diet alone cannot decide whose account of Jesus's authority is true.

Q: Is saying 'God willing' really in the Bible?
A: Yes. James 4:15 instructs believers to say, 'If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.'

Q: Does this comparison prove Islam is true?
A: No. Similar practices make Islamic continuity plausible, but truth also depends on Jesus's identity, Muhammad's prophethood, and the Quran's authority. Christians can explain changed practices through their new-covenant theology; that account must be examined on its merits.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:

- **The Muslim Jesus: Sayings and Stories in Islamic Literature** — Tarif Khalidi. How Jesus is loved, quoted, and remembered inside the Islamic tradition.
- **Jesus the Jew: A Historian's Reading of the Gospels** — Geza Vermes. A classic academic study of Jesus within the Judaism of his time.
- **The Historical Figure of Jesus** — E. P. Sanders. An accessible historical portrait of Jesus's life and practice.
- **The Imitation of Christ** — Thomas a Kempis. The most famous Christian statement of what imitating Jesus has meant.
- **Mere Christianity** — C. S. Lewis. A popular presentation of the mainstream Christian understanding of following Christ.

quranVerses.arabic: قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى يُحْبِبْكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوٓا۟ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّۦنَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ۖ فَـَٔامَنَت طَّآئِفَةٌۭ مِّنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَكَفَرَت طَّآئِفَةٌۭ ۖ فَأَيَّدْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ عَلَىٰ عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ ظَٰهِرِينَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my supporters for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ قَالَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: But when Jesus felt [persistence in] disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters for Allah. We have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى ٱلْحَوَارِيِّۦنَ أَنْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِى وَبِرَسُولِى قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And [remember] when I inspired to the disciples, "Believe in Me and in My messenger Jesus." They said, "We have believed, so bear witness that indeed we are Muslims [in submission to Allah]."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَجَعَلَنِى مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَٰنِى بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَا۟ىْءٍ إِنِّى فَاعِلٌۭ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا
quranVerses.translation: And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,"
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ۚ وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ وَقُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّى لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَٰذَا رَشَدًۭا
quranVerses.translation: Except [when adding], "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget [it] and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”

“Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward. But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does, so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
“Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.

When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
“Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”
